target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2023 disclosure (D137) covers general cybersecurity risks, persistent attacks, and the increasing sophistication of threats including AI. The 2024 disclosures are split: D134 covers the general persistent threats and attack vectors, while D135 specifically details the role of emerging technologies (AI) and generative AI in creating new attack surfaces. Both 2024 disclosures map to the specific topics contained in the single 2023 disclosure. Splitting them reflects the granular structure of the 2024 filing while maintaining the subject match.

comparisons.peer_topic: AI Software Ecosystem and Silo AI Acquisition
comparisons.peer_summary: To support its AI strategy, AMD consolidated AI teams to develop a comprehensive software ecosystem, improved AMD ROCm software performance, and acquired Silo AI Oy to accelerate AI model development and deployment on AMD hardware, leveraging Silo's software stack for training large language models.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD highlight the strategic importance of generative AI, but focus on different aspects of the ecosystem: Intel discloses AI as a source of cybersecurity risk due to the internal adoption of these technologies, whereas AMD discloses AI as a business growth driver through software optimization and acquisitions. Intel warns that its internal use of generative AI creates new attack surfaces for threat actors to exploit ('increased adoption of generative AI models within our internal systems... may create new attack methods'), while AMD emphasizes building a comprehensive software ecosystem and acquiring Silo AI to accelerate AI model development and deployment on its hardware ('brought together multiple AI teams... to drive development of a comprehensive software ecosystem... acquisition of Silo AI enables customers to accelerate development and deployment of AI models on AMD hardware').

sentences.text: Moreover, the increased adoption of generative AI models within our internal systems, processes, and tools may create new attack methods for threat actors.
To execute our AI strategy, we brought together multiple AI teams across AMD to drive development of a comprehensive software ecosystem spanning our full product portfolio.
The acquisition of Silo AI enables customers to accelerate development and deployment of AI models on AMD hardware.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates for Broadcom focus on general technology leadership via acquisitions (D004) and broad factors affecting product demand such as AI-related demand trends and cloud shifts (D005). Neither candidate addresses cybersecurity threats, AI-driven hacking sophistication, or the specific risk of internal AI adoption creating attack surfaces as disclosed by Intel. The generic mention of 'AI-related demand' in D005 is not substantively comparable to the specific operational and security risks Intel details.

The retrieved candidates for Micron focus on financial performance drivers (D005) and capital expenditure estimates (D030). There is no discussion of cybersecurity, AI-enabled threats, or internal AI security risks in these disclosures, making them unrelated to Intel's topic of AI-enhanced cyber threats.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center AI Inference Platforms and Cloud Services
comparisons.peer_summary: The company launched AI inference platforms combining software with Ada, Hopper, and Grace Hopper processors for generative AI and LLMs. It also introduced NVIDIA DGX Cloud and AI Foundations to help businesses create and operate custom large language models.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose activities related to generative AI infrastructure, but Intel frames it as a security risk while NVIDIA frames it as a product opportunity. Intel identifies that the proliferation of generative AI allows threat actors to impersonate individuals and develop hacking tools, noting that its own adoption of these models increases internal risk ('proliferation of generative AI increases the risk of these technologies being used by threat actors to impersonate authorized individuals... increased adoption of generative AI models within our internal systems... may create new attack methods'). In contrast, NVIDIA highlights the launch of specific AI inference platforms and cloud services designed to help businesses create and operate custom large language models and generative AI models ('In Data Center, we launched AI inference platforms that combine our full-stack inference software... optimized for generative AI, LLMs... We introduced NVIDIA DGX Cloud and AI Foundations to help businesses create and operate custom large language models and generative AI models').

sentences.text: The proliferation of generative AI increases the risk of these technologies being used by threat actors to impersonate authorized individuals, which may make attacks even more difficult to detect and prevent.
Moreover, the increased adoption of generative AI models within our internal systems, processes, and tools may create new attack methods for threat actors.

In Data Center, we launched AI inference platforms that combine our full-stack inference software with NVIDIA Ada, NVIDIA Hopper and NVIDIA Grace Hopper processors optimized for generative AI, LLMs and other AI workloads.
We introduced NVIDIA DGX Cloud and AI Foundations to help businesses create and operate custom large language models and generative AI models.
